title: Retention execution tracing and evidentiary export driver
creator: Aisha Nadeem
description: Build a deterministic execution tracer for retention policy evaluations and a pluggable evidentiary export driver. The tracer must capture the policy decision path for each request (route/model/tenant/flags), the TTL resolution steps, sampling decisions, and the resulting storage action (retain/purge/archive/sample). The export driver will assemble a signed evidence bundle per legal/forensic request, containing the traced decision graph, policy versions, cryptographic hashes of artifacts, and the minimum artifact set required (prompts, responses, request-log pointers, metric rollups). This ticket implements the core engine components and integration points, not the UI for exploring traces.
background: Customers and audit teams require not only that retention rules are applied, but that each enforcement decision can be explained and reproduced. Current retention systems produce asynchronous evidentiary exports but lack per-request decision traces and verifiable bindings between policy versions and retained artifacts. This gap complicates legal holds and compliance investigations.
goals: Produce a per-request retention decision trace that records inputs, policy evaluation steps, intermediate TTL computations, and final action
Provide an exportable evidence bundle format (signed JSON + attachments) usable by auditors and legal teams
Design a pluggable driver interface so Dedicated/Private deployments can swap storage/export backends
Ensure low overhead for hot-path requests: trace should be sampled and/or lightweight when not requested
Include end-to-end tests and a small reference UI hook for QA (internal only)
non_goals: Full console trace explorer (will be follow-on PM work)
Long-term archival storage implementation (we will integrate existing archivers)
Large-scale rehydration or replay tooling (out of scope)
acceptance_criteria: API: retention tracer emits standardized trace object for every evaluated request when tracing enabled
Export: evidence driver can build a signed bundle containing trace.json, policy-manifest.json, artifact-references.txt, and cryptographic hashes
Performance: tracer disabled by default; when enabled for 1% sampling, p50 request latency increase <2ms and p95 <5ms in local perf tests
Compatibility: driver interface implemented for S3-compatible store and local FS (for on-prem demo)
Auditability: policy-manifest includes policy id, semantic diff from last deployed version, and operator who changed it
implementation_plan: Design trace schema and versioning (trace-v1) — include fields for request_id, route_id, tenant_id, timestamp, policy_evaluations[]
Add lightweight in-memory trace builder in runtime; make it NoOp when tracer disabled
Create Export Driver interface (IRetentionEvidenceDriver) with methods: assembleBundle, signBundle, pushBundle
Wire tracer to retention pipeline and sampling config; expose internal flag for QA
Add unit/integration tests and microbenchmark harness; run on runtime-1.23 perf rack
Small reference playbook and QA checklist for Solutions/SE to exercise evidence exports
design_decisions: Trace recorded as an append-only JSON graph instead of relational rows to keep bundle self-contained
Use ed25519 keys for bundle signing (key rotation planned in a follow-up ticket)
Sampling controlled via config per-route with probabilistic and deterministic (trace-nth) modes
Artifacts inside bundles are referenced by immutable storage pointers and accompanied by SHA256 hashes rather than embedding large binaries by default
